aria: Animated recap of the Trail Blazers' 120 to 107 road win over the Kings: Deni Avdija's 27-foot pull-up three with 7:18 left that made it 108 to 96 after a Sacramento run, quarter-by-quarter scoring, Avdija's 34 points on 11-of-13 shooting, the top scorers, how the Blazers won, and the next game at Minnesota.
notes: Box score from the Trail Blazers' 120–107 win over the Sacramento Kings at Golden 1 Center on Nov 13, 2026, an NBA Cup group game, from the StatMuse box score and play log, with game details from the Associated Press (via CBS Sacramento and KATU), Field Level Media (via The Ticket and 95.3 The Score), Sports Radio Service, Sactown Sports, Yahoo Sports and Blazers on SI. All 120 Portland points and all 107 Sacramento points are accounted for in the box score, and the quarter scores add up to both totals: 64–53 Portland at the half and 93–78 after three (StatMuse). Biggest leads: Portland 20 (98–78 early in the fourth), Sacramento 5 (StatMuse). Team stats are StatMuse's; bench points (27–17) also match Field Level Media. Records and ranks are from the site's standings (data/season.json) after Friday's games.

Avdija scored 34 on 11-of-13 shooting and 9 of 9 at the line, with 14 in the fourth quarter (StatMuse play log; Blazers on SI). Damian Lillard had 29, all six of his field goals threes, and went 11 of 11 at the line, 22 of his points in the second half (StatMuse; Blazers on SI). Portland never trailed in the second half (Field Level Media), and made 17 threes to Sacramento's 11 and 29 of 31 free throws. It is Portland's third straight win; the Blazers are 6–1 on the road, and Sacramento has lost five straight (AP). Portland plays at Minnesota on Monday at 8:00 PM ET (Yardbarker; Covers).

How it was decided: Portland led 102–84 early in the fourth before Sacramento scored 12 of the next 15, seven of them in 56 seconds by Darius Acuff Jr., to get within 105–96 at 7:36 (StatMuse play log; Yahoo Sports). Avdija answered with a three and a driving layup (110–96 at 6:41), Lillard hit a 28-foot pull-up three at 5:34 (113–98), and Lillard's three free throws at 3:35 made it 116–103 (StatMuse; Sports Radio Service).

The play of the game is an original illustration of Avdija's 27-foot pull-up three with 7:18 left, which made it 108–96 (StatMuse play log: "D. Avdija 27' pullup three"; Sports Radio Service: "Avdija's three and driving layup pushed it to 110-96"). The figures are stylized and not traced from footage, and the spacing is not to scale.

The music is an original beat made for this page. No existing recordings or melodies are used. This is an unofficial fan recap, not affiliated with the Portland Trail Blazers or the NBA, which is why it carries a plain basketball mark and the team's colors but not the team's logo.

The player in the play of the game is drawn to Avdija's listed 6-foot-8 and 228 pounds (CBS Sports); no wingspan from an approved source was found, so his arms are drawn in proportion to his height. He is in Portland's road red with No. 8 (CBS Sports). He has no approved look on file yet, so he is drawn as a team-colour silhouette in the kit. It is an original silhouette with a featureless face, not a portrait or a trace of footage.
